2608.11204.title: Surgical WAM: A World-Action Model for Data-Efficient Surgical Robot Learning
2608.11204.paper_summary: Learning reliable surgical manipulation policies is bottlenecked by the scarcity of action-labeled demonstrations: teleoperated surgical robot (e.g., dVRK) trajectories with synchronized kinematics are costly to collect, while surgical tasks demand precise contact handling, long-horizon reasoning, and bimanual coordination. Endoscopic video is comparatively inexpensive and abundant relative to synchronized video--kinematics trajectories, and a natural way to exploit it is to learn world models of surgical scenes. However, existing surgical world models use video primarily for simulation or policy evaluation, and rarely translate the learned dynamics into closed-loop control. This gap raises our central question: under a fixed budget of action-labeled demonstrations, does action-free video pretraining improve closed-loop surgical manipulation? To answer it, we introduce the Surgical World-Action Model (Surgical WAM), a unified generative model built on Cosmos Policy that jointly predicts future endoscopic observations and executable surgical robot action chunks. Surgical WAM first learns surgical visual dynamics from action-free video and is then fine-tuned on the fixed action-labeled budget; at deployment, it acts as a closed-loop, receding-horizon controller that executes a short prefix of each predicted action chunk and replans from the resulting observation. On a suite of four simulated surgical manipulation tasks, video pretraining improves the average success rate from 63.5% to 77.8%, including an absolute gain of 20 percentage points on PegTransfer, with the largest improvements on contact-rich and bimanual tasks. These results demonstrate that action-free video provides transferable visual dynamics priors for learning surgical robot control with limited action supervision, positioning data-efficient video pretraining as a practical path toward scaling up surgical robot learning.
2608.11204.paper_summary_zh: 學習可靠的手術操作策略受到動作標記示範稀缺的瓶頸：遠程操作的手術機器人（例如，dVRK）與同步運動學的軌跡收集成本高昂，而手術任務則需要精確的接觸處理、長期推理和雙手協調。相較於同步視頻—運動學軌跡，內視鏡視頻相對便宜且豐富，利用它的自然方式是學習手術場景的世界模型。然而，現有的手術世界模型主要將視頻用於模擬或策略評估，並且很少將學習到的動態轉化為閉環控制。這一差距引出了我們的核心問題：在固定的動作標記示範預算下，無動作視頻的預訓練是否能改善閉環手術操作？為了解答這個問題，我們提出了手術世界-動作模型（Surgical WAM），這是一個基於Cosmos Policy的統一生成模型，能夠共同預測未來的內視鏡觀察和可執行的手術機器人動作片段。手術WAM首先從無動作視頻中學習手術視覺動態，然後在固定的動作標記預算上進行微調；在部署時，它作為一個閉環、逐步推進的控制器，執行每個預測動作片段的短前綴，並根據結果觀察重新規劃。在四個模擬手術操作任務的測試中，視頻預訓練將平均成功率從63.5%提高到77.8%，包括在PegTransfer上獲得20個百分點的絕對增益，並在接觸豐富和雙手任務上獲得最大的改善。這些結果表明，無動作視頻為在有限動作監督下學習手術機器人控制提供了可轉移的視覺動態先驗，將數據高效的視頻預訓練定位為擴大手術機器人學習的實用途徑。
